correctness.rationale: I reconstructed F(k) as fourth divided difference of exp at z_j=-2πi times the five integer nodes; the unnormalized simplex volume is 1/24 at zero, fixing normalizations. For distinct nodes exp(z_j)=1 gives zero divided difference. For repetitions, confluent residues yield a rational polynomial P(s) in s=i/(2π); transcendence of π prevents accidental vanishing of a nonzero rational polynomial. Partition enumeration of 5 identifies every pattern with a unique largest multiplicity: its lowest s degree has a single nonzero term. Only multiplicity 2+2+1 can cancel, and its s³ coefficient vanishes precisely when the singleton equals the midpoint of the repeated endpoints. I independently reconstructed the residue polynomial for all 210 multisets drawn from -3..3 containing zero, with exactly 15 all-distinct and 5 repeated zeros. Symbolic residue cancellation for symmetric {-h,-h,0,h,h} proves sufficiency for all integer gaps; the 2+2 pattern in smaller simplex dimensions gives nonzero s coefficient. The finite test supports, but is not the infinite proof.
residual_risks: Restricted to integer lattice and standard simplex; not a classification over real frequencies or dimensions≥5.

value.rationale: The standard simplex is canonical in Fourier analysis, and its discrete zero set is central to harmonic tilings and sampling. The first repeated-node resonance is an exact structural boundary distinguishing distinct-phase cancellation from nontrivial confluent cancellation. Classifying all Z⁴ zeros is a mathematically motivated complete invariant, not an arbitrary finite list.
residual_risks: No arbitrary affine-simplex or higher-dimension classification is claimed.

final_claim: For the standard Euclidean 4-simplex, its Fourier transform at integer k vanishes exactly when the five vertex phase nodes {0,k1,k2,k3,k4} are distinct or form an arithmetic progression with multiplicities 2,1,2, the first simplex dimension permitting a repeated-node lattice zero.
limitations: Unnormalized Fourier transform with frequency -2πi convention.
The 210-case finite residue census is diagnostic only.
